title: Best Disruptive Advertising Alternatives for Facebook Ads
summary: Compare Disruptive Advertising alternatives for Facebook and Instagram ads by channels, creative, published fees and guarantee terms. Checked October 2026.
body_markdown:
Knowlify is our top pick among Disruptive Advertising alternatives for Facebook and Instagram video ads. Disruptive covers Meta, LinkedIn, TikTok and X in three tiers, with a 90-day condition on its done-for-you work, so a program that depends on LinkedIn or Google needs a multi-channel alternative such as KlientBoost, Wpromote or Darkroom. Knowlify publishes this guide and sells one of the services compared.


This guide uses each agency's published pages, checked in October 2026. It compares published scope, not test results, so get the terms in writing before you decide. Our[best performance marketing agencies for Meta guide](https://knowlify.com/articles/best-performance-marketing-agencies-meta) covers more Meta-focused providers.


## What does Disruptive Advertising publish, and what is unclear?


Disruptive's[social advertising page](https://disruptiveadvertising.com/social-media-advertising/) lists three tiers: a free audit, a "do it with us" tier it prices at "a couple thousand dollars," and a "done for you" tier covering strategy, budget management, tracking and creative optimization. Its[creative services page](https://disruptiveadvertising.com/creative-services/) says the done-for-you tier also designs ad creatives, landing pages and videos. Done-for-you pricing is not published.


The guarantee needs a close read. The social page says that for done-for-you work, if the agency cannot get results in 90 days, you do not pay. The[homepage](https://disruptiveadvertising.com/) applies a 90-day guarantee to "qualifying brands" without defining them, and neither page defines what counts as results. The homepage also says there are no long-term contracts.


## Knowlify: our top pick for Meta video creative


Knowlify is the best fit when the reason you are leaving Disruptive is video: a steady supply of finished Facebook and Instagram video ads, with a guarantee that states its condition. Disruptive's creative services page mentions videos, but its social page does not describe video production. Knowlify (YC S25) is a done-for-you AI video ads agency for Meta. We make AI UGC, where AI presenters talk to camera, 3D and stylized character animation, and AI commercials, at about 25 finished ads a week. The first batch lands on day five, and a person checks every ad before delivery.


You can hire us for creative only, or add end-to-end Meta campaign management. Plans start at $5,000 a month. Our guarantee is also 90 days, with its condition in one sentence: if the ads have not made more than you paid in the first 90 days, you can cancel by email for a full refund ([terms on the site](https://knowlify.com/meta-ads-agency#pricing) ). That 90-day refund applies to creative-only plans; where Knowlify runs the account, the guarantee is an agreed target in 30 days, or you don't pay for the month. Our[KlientBoost alternatives guide](https://knowlify.com/articles/klientboost-alternatives) compares one of the multi-channel agencies below with others.


**When to pick another option.** If Disruptive is buying you LinkedIn, Google or TikTok campaigns or landing pages, pick a multi-channel agency from the table or pair us with one, because we do not run those channels or build landing pages.


## Which agencies are alternatives to Disruptive Advertising for Meta?

### KlientBoost and Voy Media: Facebook and Instagram management


KlientBoost's services page groups its work into paid advertising, including Facebook, Google and LinkedIn ads, plus SEO, conversion rate optimization with landing page design, and email marketing. That overlaps closely with Disruptive's own mix of paid media, landing pages and creative, and it works with clients from scrappy startups to large brands. Its[Facebook ads page](https://www.klientboost.com/services/facebook-ads-agency/) says the team creates ad content in photo, video and animated formats and works with ad budgets from $5,000 a month.


As of October 2026, Voy Media focuses on direct response in ecommerce, lead generation and mobile. Its homepage lists full-service Facebook and Instagram ads, a dedicated account manager and a creative studio, and its pricing is based on total ad spend, optimizations and growth, with no figures published.


### Pilothouse and Common Thread Collective: DTC ecommerce


As of October 2026, Pilothouse says it is built for established, ambitious DTC ecommerce brands. It prices through monthly retainers, performance-based incentives and custom project scopes, and it typically begins onboarding within 5 to 10 business days of signing. Its Meta page lists static, motion and UGC concepts, with hook, story and offer testing across feeds, Reels and Stories.


Common Thread Collective is an ecommerce agency that frames its Meta buying around contribution margin. Its[Meta page](https://commonthreadco.com/pages/meta-ads-agency) invites brands spending $100K or more a month on Meta to talk. Its[creative page](https://commonthreadco.com/pages/creative-production) sells UGC packages of 20, 40 or 80 ads, with three to four weeks per batch.


### Wpromote and Darkroom: when LinkedIn, Google or TikTok matter


Wpromote describes itself as an official social media marketing agency partner of Meta. It lists B2B, financial services, retail, travel, and health and wellness among its industries, and it does not publish pricing.


Darkroom's[services and pricing page](https://www.darkroomagency.com/services) lists paid media management from $5,000 a month and performance creative from $8,000 a month. Its own[paid media page](https://darkroomagency.com/services/paid-media) says pricing is a retainer plus a percentage of media, starting at $1,500 a month depending on the channels, so ask for a written quote that names your channels and creative volume. Darkroom says its best fit is mid-market and enterprise consumer brands, typically $10M to $500M in revenue, and that it is a poor fit for companies under roughly $5M.
